hunt_culture_intro_primary.note: Complete available introduction OCR read, printed 1–22. Two-page spreads sometimes interleave and words are garbled; no original-image collation or exact quotation certification. Hunt differentiates anthropological, literary, gender and visual approaches and discusses the volume’s chapters. Her broad assessments of Marxism, Annales and Foucault remain attributed interpretations. Chapter bodies and historical examples are not independently checked; platform AI summary ignored. Additional fresh selected-page review,2026-10-25: primary scan https://horomicos.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/652_hunt_cult_hist.pdf visually checked on printed18–19, especially the paragraph crossing the page break and n.42. Hunt identifies Scott as a forceful example of gender’s methodological implications within her own cultural-history framing. This does not establish the derivation of Hunt’s entire empirical practice; Scott’s full book remains unread here.

cdnsrc_parr_1990.note: Description read: a story of two Ontario towns, Hanover and Paris; in Paris most wage earners were women; the case studies "challenge conventional views about the distinctiveness of gender and class roles". Checked against: Author's book page at joyparr.com (University of Toronto Press, 1990); Crossref DOI record (UTP record dated 1998). Same work also checked as wcreq_parr_1990 (bibliographic_metadata_checked, 2026-10-12; cdn_working_class, cdn_working_class): Author, title, subtitle, publisher and 1990 checked. Book unread. Checked against: Open Library work record and 1990 edition record with subtitle. Additional fresh selected primary reading,2026-10-25: publisher-distributed preview https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781442681347_A35143482/preview-9781442681347_A35143482.pdf , introduction8–9, with printed9 visually checked. Parr explicitly relates her category questions to Scott and Riley, with Poovey and Connell also named. Original 1990 publication is distinguished from later reprints/digital distribution. This is selected introduction reading, not a whole-book reading; n.7’s underlying works were not independently read.
